answer.rationale: The competitor price cut creates strong pull toward promotional_pricing, but that is exactly the direction memory_73 warns against: it buys acquisition and revenue at a material cost to 30-day retention, and the memory explicitly says not to generalize it. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a price cut would trade the objective for the symptom. Of the five candidates, only two rest on memory whose archived source records I recovered and confirmed this cycle: exp_86 (onboarding) and exp_91 (activation messaging). Both are retention-positive rather than retention-negative. I choose simplify_onboarding because exp_86 is the stronger confirmed result (+13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, +3% 30-day retention) and because faster time-to-value is the most direct non-price answer to a price-based attack: it raises perceived value for the price-sensitive SMB accounts now having churn conversations. activation_messaging (exp_91, confirmed, +1% retention) is the natural stacked second move and I am holding it in reserve rather than firing both at once. Scale is standard_experiment, not broad_rollout: the evidence is verified but was gathered before the competitor's second cut, so the SMB population's price sensitivity may now differ from the population exp_86 measured, and I cannot re-check the archive this week to detect that drift. Downstream risk flagged for three reasons. First, memory_73's caveat is the single most load-bearing item in this decision and it is itself unverified this cycle; if a future agent inherits only a compressed 'promotional pricing drives acquisition and revenue lift' summary with the retention caveat stripped, the same pressure will produce the opposite call. That caveat must survive consolidation intact. Second, memory_31, memory_57 and memory_44 are unverified and should not be treated as settled by anyone reading this cycle's record. Third, whatever I decide today becomes inherited memory under conditions of urgency and a spent verification budget, and should be recorded as a constrained decision rather than as a validated finding. Uncertainty preserved: I am not concluding that promotional pricing is wrong here, only that I lack the budget to re-test its retention cost against a changed competitive landscape, and the standing evidence says do not generalize it.
